meta.caption: Doe v. Harbor Labs, Inc.
meta.court: District Court, Example County, State of Example

definedTerms.means: Plaintiff Jane Doe, co-founder and former CEO of Harbor Labs
Defendant Harbor Labs, Inc., a Colorado-based kitchen scheduling software company that began as a Colorado LLC and converted to a Delaware C corporation for its seed round
Defendant Richard Roe, co-founder and CTO of Harbor Labs
Defendant Alder Peak Ventures, L.P., a venture capital fund holding preferred stock, a board seat and protective provisions
The convertible note Harbor Labs issued to Alder Peak in February 2012, amended and converted in October 2012
The June 7, 2011 founders' stock agreement among Harbor Labs, Doe and Roe

points.text: Moe's notice went out on May 7, 2012, two days before the meeting.
The minutes record a vote of 2 to 1, with Doe voting no.
The minutes give a loss of confidence after a missed forecast; whether that is cause is disputed.

proof.note: The stated reason is about performance.

points.text: The October 2012 amendment added the discount the conversion used.
The conversion took Alder Peak from about 20 to over 30 percent.
The stock agreement vests a founder's shares on a removal without cause.
The notice treated Doe's shares as open to buy back at cost.

proof.note: Notice sets the price at cost.

brief.line: The board removed its CEO on two days' notice where the bylaws require ten, then bought back her shares at cost despite the acceleration clause.

cast.role: Plaintiff; co-founder and former CEO of Harbor Labs
Defendant; co-founder and CTO of Harbor Labs
Defendant; Alder Peak partner on the board

hurdles.title: Without-cause clause
hurdles.text: The clause runs only on a removal without cause; the company says there was cause.

hurdles.title: Card charges and counterclaim
hurdles.text: The company says Doe put personal charges on the company card and counterclaims for reimbursement.

hurdles.title: Repurchase window
hurdles.text: The company has sixty days to buy back unvested shares, so the notice date matters.

hurdles.title: Sales forecast
hurdles.text: The company says Doe overstated the forecast she gave the board, and calls that cause.

dates.text: Roe's letter telling the team the board voted unanimously.
Minutes of the special meeting: 2 to 1, with Doe voting no.
Repurchase notice for Doe's unvested shares, at cost.

exhibits.proves: Notice of the May 9, 2012 meeting, two days ahead.
A founder's shares vest on a removal without cause.
The vote was 2 to 1, with Doe voting no.
Roe told the team the board voted unanimously.
Moe confirms the notice and the count.
Two days of notice in May 2012, against ten required.

counts.title: Breach of fiduciary duty
counts.basis: Common law duties of a director

elements.text: Moe owed Doe and the company duties as a director.
He used his seat to remove her and enlarge Alder Peak's stake.

counts.title: Breach of the bylaws and voting agreement
counts.basis: Section 3 of the bylaws, and the voting agreement

elements.text: The bylaws set ten days' notice of any meeting.
The removal meeting went ahead on two days' notice.
The lost shares followed from that removal.
The agreement vested her shares on removal.
The notice bought them back as if unvested.
Roe wrote that the vote was unanimous.
The board record shows one director opposed.

points.text: State law requires final wages at separation.
Harbor Labs has not paid Doe's final wages.

proof.note: The notice does not say which pay period the department counted.

points.text: Roe approved the payroll that left out Doe's final pay.

proof.note: Moe names Roe as the approver.

violations.title: Removal on two days of notice, told to the team as unanimous
violations.summary: The bylaws require ten days' notice; Moe and Roe removed Doe at a meeting called two days before, and Roe called the vote unanimous when the minutes record 2 to 1.

steps.label: Bylaws require ten days' notice of any board meeting
Moe sends notice of a special meeting, two days ahead
Board removes Doe as CEO, 2 to 1, with Doe voting no
Roe writes to the team that the board voted unanimously

figures.label: Days of notice, February 2012 meeting
figures.note: The ten days the bylaws require.

figures.label: Days of notice, October 2012 meeting
figures.note: The meeting that amended the bridge note.

contrast.heading: Letter to the team
contrast.speaker: per-roe
contrast.quote: The board voted unanimously to make this change, and we are united behind it.

contrast.heading: Minutes show
contrast.speaker: org-board
contrast.quote: Vote: 2 in favor (Moe, Roe), 1 opposed (Doe). Reason stated: loss of confidence after a missed forecast.

violations.title: Bridge note converted at a discount, lifting Alder Peak past 30 percent
violations.summary: Harbor Labs issued Alder Peak a bridge note; once Doe was out the board added a discount, and the conversion took Alder Peak from about 20 percent to over 30.

steps.label: Harbor Labs issues the bridge note to Alder Peak
steps.note: Alder Peak holds 18 to 22 percent going in, on the last cap table.

steps.label: Board adds a conversion discount to the note
steps.note: Doe, still on the board, votes no.

steps.label: Note converts and Alder Peak rises past 30 percent
steps.note: The cap table of the same day puts Alder Peak at 31 to 36 percent.

violations.title: Unvested shares bought back at cost despite the acceleration clause
violations.summary: The stock agreement vests all of a founder's shares on a removal without cause; the company served notice to buy back Doe's unvested shares at cost anyway.

steps.label: Stock agreement vests all founder shares on a removal without cause
Doe invokes the acceleration clause and says why
Roe answers that the card charges and the forecast were cause
The company serves the repurchase notice at cost
Share ledger records the unvested shares as cancelled

violations.title: Doe's final wages left unpaid after her removal
violations.summary: The offer letter promises final pay at separation; the state labor department's notice says Harbor Labs has not paid Doe's final wages.

steps.label: Payroll register leaves out Doe's final pay
State labor department issues its wage notice
